title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: handle waiting conversations when a queue closes or has no representatives signed in
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, waiting-conversation conditions, roles and publishing charges are supported by Microsoft documentation. Minor corrections should clarify where the editor path ends and which API properties configure the record, align the risk rationale with the opt-in default, and identify the billing checklist step that has no controls-table row.

claims.claim: The Queue page's out-of-operating-hours overflow rule is evaluated once before queue entry, not when the queue closes around already-waiting conversations.

claims.claim: Representative-availability overflow can trigger immediately instead of waiting for time or volume-based conditions.
claims.quote: Configure overflow handling to trigger immediately when eligible service representatives aren't available for a work item or queues are out of operating hours, instead of waiting for time or volume-based conditions.

claims.claim: Without overflow handling, a work item is added to the queue and the customer waits for a representative.
claims.quote: If you don't set up overflow handling, then by default, the work item is added to the queue and the customer waits to be connected to a service representative.
